comparator.name: International Relations and International Organization
comparator.sourceNotes: The curriculum follows the redesigned regular programme for students starting in 2026–2027. The first two years each carry 60 EC and include two linked modern-language courses. Year three contains a 30 EC minor, a 10 EC Faculty-Wide Course II choice, a 10 EC specialization module and a 10 EC thesis.
components: Historical Foundations of Modern International Relations
Political Systems in the World: Foundations of Political Science
Analyzing International Relations: Theories and Approaches
EU Politics and Law in Global Perspective
Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis

core: International relations, international organisations, global politics and cross-border interdependence
European Union politics, institutions, populism and Euroscepticism
International law, international economics and global political economy
International security, war, conflict and peace
Global and diplomatic history and comparison of political systems
Compulsory modern-language training for international affairs
Independent research, methodology, statistics and data analysis in international relations
adjacent: International security, international law and data-informed global governance
International cooperation on climate change and global environmental governance
questions: Why do countries struggle to cooperate on shared environmental problems?

alternatives.label: International Relations, Organisations and Political Economy
alternatives.labelReason: Political philosophy, legal foundations and research methods precede advanced European politics, EU law, econometrics and conflict analysis.
alternatives.concept: Study how states and international organisations make decisions, cooperate and respond to conflict. International relations theory, European politics, law and global history sit alongside political economy and research methods.
progression: Political philosophy, legal foundations and research methods precede advanced European politics, EU law, econometrics and conflict analysis.
traceOverrides: compares policy processes across levels and uses policy memos to evaluate responses to cross-border problems

alternatives.label: International Security, Law and Governance
alternatives.labelReason: Foundations in politics, law and history precede criminal justice, conflict and radicalisation, with quantitative and qualitative methods and a history research seminar.
alternatives.concept: Study how conflict develops and how institutions respond. Peacebuilding, international and criminal law, the history of warfare and research on radicalisation connect questions of security to rights and governance.
progression: Foundations in politics, law and history precede criminal justice, conflict and radicalisation, with quantitative and qualitative methods and a history research seminar.
alternatives.distinctness: Criminal justice, radicalisation, moral reasoning and historical research give this option a security focus.
traceOverrides: compares policy processes across levels and uses policy memos to evaluate responses to cross-border problems

alternatives.label: Climate Governance and International Cooperation
alternatives.labelReason: Sustainability and research foundations support renewable system design, policy analysis and resource recovery. Nature-based infrastructure precedes applied water governance.
alternatives.concept: Study how governments and communities respond to climate change across borders. International law and policy connect to renewable energy, water governance, environmental justice and public debate.
progression: Sustainability and research foundations support renewable system design, policy analysis and resource recovery. Nature-based infrastructure precedes applied water governance.
alternatives.distinctness: Climate science, water governance, renewable energy, resource recovery and environmental justice shape this option.
traceOverrides: compares policy processes across levels and uses policy memos to evaluate responses to cross-border problems

candidates.label: Modern Foreign-Language Study for International Affairs

selection.assessment: The broad comparison, security concentration and climate governance concentration differ pairwise by 37.5, 97.5 and 105 EC each way. Introductory Dutch contributes language exposure, but the active course set cannot support a separate language-centred programme or the comparator’s two linked proficiency courses. Three distinct options reach the maximum.

blocks: Students choose a 30 EC minor, with approval where required.
Students choose one of four faculty-wide courses. The topics depend on their choice.
International relations, organisations and political systems
Both compare political institutions, regime types and political participation.
Both use international relations theories to analyse state behaviour, cooperation and conflict.
Both study European Union institutions and decision-making. Groningen also integrates EU law in this course.
Groningen requires a separate introduction before its theory course. UCR’s theory course covers some introductory ground.
Groningen gives current international affairs a separate course.
Law, European governance, security and conflict
Both study treaties, state responsibilities and the role of international organisations.
Both examine causes of armed conflict, security and responses to violence. UCR gives particular attention to peacebuilding.
Both introduce how markets work and how policy affects economic outcomes.
Both examine economic interdependence across borders. UCR focuses on macroeconomics, while Groningen studies the politics of the global economy.
Both cover historical changes that shape world politics, including war, decolonisation and globalisation.
Both use the history of power across borders to explain the present. UCR focuses on empires.
The specialization module focuses on an international relations theme and prepares students for the linked thesis.
Groningen requires a thesis linked to the specialization module. Independent research at UCR is optional.
Both introduce statistical reasoning for empirical questions. UCR also teaches research design.
Both teach research design and methods. UCR focuses on qualitative social research, while Groningen applies methods to international relations.
Groningen requires the first course in a modern-language sequence. UCR offers introductory Dutch.
Groningen normally continues the same language. The UCR options have no equivalent progression.
Groningen studies global change through several perspectives. UCR’s climate courses address environmental change and its consequences.

notes.text: Groningen requires two linked modern-language courses and a dedicated sequence in international relations. UCR offers related study across politics, law, economics, history and social research.
Groningen sets aside 30 EC for a minor and requires a faculty-wide course, a specialization module and a linked thesis. UCR students can pursue independent research as an option.

audience.programmeDescription: International Relations and International Organization at the University of Groningen studies power, cooperation and conflict across borders. Students study politics, history, law and economics, develop research skills and continue a modern language across two years.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines politics, law, history and political economy. The other options concentrate on international security or climate governance. Groningen requires a two-course language sequence, an international relations specialization and a linked thesis. UCR offers introductory Dutch and optional independent research.
